cards.title: Looping over a dictionary
cards.body: `for key in d` visits the keys in the order they were added. `d.items()` gives each key and value together.

hi.title: Dictionary par loop
hi.body: `for key in d` keys par usi order mein jaata hai jismein woh jodi gayi thi. `d.items()` har key aur value ek saath deta hai.

cards.title: The best so far
cards.body: Keep the best value seen so far and replace it only when you find something strictly better. `None` means "nothing yet". Using `>` rather than `>=` keeps the first one on a tie.

hi.title: Ab tak ka best
hi.body: Ab tak ki best value rakho aur use tabhi badlo jab kuch sach mein behtar mile. `None` ka matlab "abhi kuch nahi". `>=` ki jagah `>` use karne se tie hone par pehla wala bana rehta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print each name with its score, but crashes with a `ValueError`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Looping over a dictionary gives only its keys. Use `scores.items()` to get each name and score together.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse har naam uske score ke saath print karna chahiye, par yeh `ValueError` dekar crash hota hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Dictionary par loop sirf keys deta hai. Har naam aur score ek saath paane ke liye `scores.items()` use karo.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: best becomes 3, then 7. The second 7 is not greater, and 1 is smaller.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: best pehle 3 banta hai, phir 7. Doosra 7 bada nahi hai, aur 1 chhota hai.

exercise.prompt: The first line is a count N; then N lines of `name score`. Print the name with the highest score. If several share it, print the one that came first.
exercise.promptHi: Pehli line mein count N hai; phir `name score` ki N lines. Sabse zyada score wala naam print karo. Agar kai logon ka same ho, toh jo pehle aaya woh print karo.
